Systems Engineers apply a structured approach to the design and implementation of system and service applications. They capture and translate mission and customer requirements into capabilities using the System Development Lifecycle (SDLC).

Systems Engineers analyze and allocate requirements to systems architecture components and oversee the design, development, testing, and validation of systems and services. They also coordinate the integration of systems and services into enterprise architecture and oversee deployment.
MANDATORY QUALIFICATION CRITERIA: For this particular job, applicants must meet all competencies reflected under the Mandatory Qualification Criteria to include education (if required).

Online resumes must demonstrate qualification by providing specific examples and associated results, in response to the announcement's mandatory criteria specified in this vacancy announcement: Demonstrated experience in technical planning across the full lifecycle of an engineering project such as understanding the deliverables; executing project plans; communicating progress; generating requirements, test and evaluation (T&E) of systems and/or facilitating problem resolutions.

Demonstrated end-to-end understanding of the systems development lifecycle (SDLC) methodologies and processes for planning, designing, developing, testing, and/or deploying a system.

Demonstrated experience with managing a configuration management database to include but not limited to documenting and/or addressing baseline configuration & system changes or deviations.

Experience with integration efforts in a collaborative environment for components and data of complex systems/applications, ensuring adaptability for future architecture design. EDUCATION REQUIREMENT: A.

Education: Bachelor's degree or higher from an accredited college or university in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Engineering, Engineering Management, Information Science, Information Systems Management, Information Technology, Mathematics, Operations Research, Statistics, Technology Management, System Engineering, or a degree that provided a minimum of 24 semester hours in one or more of the fields identified above and required the development or adaptation of applications, systems, or networks. -OR- B.

Combination of Education and Experience: A minimum of 24 semester (36 quarter) hours of coursework in any area listed in option A, plus experience in Information Technology, systems planning, research, development, engineering, or a related area that demonstrates the ability to successfully perform the duties associated with this work.

As a rule, every 30 semester (45 quarter) hours of coursework is equivalent to one year of experience. Candidates should show that their combination of education and experience totals 4 years. -OR- C.

Experience: A minimum of 4 years of experience in Information Technology, systems planning, research, development, engineering, or a related area that demonstrates the ability to successfully perform the duties associated with this work. -AND- LICENSES/CERTIFICATIONS: DAWIA Certification may be required for this position; See Position License and Certification Requirements for additional details.

New Acquisition Workforce members or members transferring to a different or higher skill level -AND- Relevant Competencies: IT-related experience demonstrating each of the four competencies: Attention to Detail, Customer Service, Oral Communication, and Problem Solving.

DESIRABLE QUALIFICATION CRITERIA: In addition to the mandatory qualifications, experience in the following is desired: Experience with Imagery, Sensor, or GIS Data Technologies.

Experience leading teams who perform test and evaluation for GEOINT sensor technologies such as Electro Optical (EO), Synthetic Aperture RADAR (SAR), Hyperspectral, or motion video. Experience with ITIL/IT Service Management and/or Agile, SAFe, Waterfall, or Spiral development and the tools used to manage them.

Experience with engineering solutions in Service Centric Architecture, Cloud-based technologies, structured or unstructured Big Data, and/or Artificial Intelligence.

Ihre Karriere im Bereich Automotive Power Electronic.
Mit BRÜGGEN ENGINEERING entwickeln Sie die Systeminfrastruktur moderner Hochvolt-Invertersysteme für hybride und vollelektrische Fahrzeuge. Sie übernehmen die technische Verantwortung für Systemfunktionen, koordinieren interdisziplinäre Entwicklungsteams und gestalten gemeinsam mit Kunden robuste und zukunftsfähige Systemlösungen.
Aufgaben
Systementwicklung: Sie verantworten die Entwicklung und Umsetzung von Systeminfrastrukturfunktionen für Hochvolt-Inverter über den gesamten Produktlebenszyklus.
Systemkonzepte: Sie entwickeln robuste Konzepte und Anforderungen unter Berücksichtigung von Qualität, Leistung, Kosten und Terminen.
Koordination: Sie steuern die Zusammenarbeit zwischen Hardware, Software, Kalibrierung, Safety und Test.
Kundenkommunikation: Sie führen technische Abstimmungen und fungieren als zentrale Ansprechperson für die verantworteten Funktionen.
Fehleranalyse: Sie identifizieren Ursachen technischer Probleme und entwickeln wirksame Lösungen auf Systemebene.
Funktionale Sicherheit: Sie unterstützen Sicherheitskonzepte, SFMEA und FTA gemäß ISO 26262.
Projektsteuerung: Sie berichten über Status, Risiken und Maßnahmen und unterstützen die fachliche Führung der Projektteams.
Qualifikation
Qualifikation: Abgeschlossenes Masterstudium in Fahrzeugtechnik, Elektrotechnik, Elektronik, Mechatronik oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung
Erfahrung: Mindestens zehn Jahre Berufserfahrung in der automobilen Systementwicklung, idealerweise im Bereich Hochvolt-Inverter, Leistungselektronik oder elektrifizierte Antriebe
Systemengineering: Fundierte Kenntnisse in den Bereichen Anforderungsentwicklung, Systemarchitektur, Integration, Verifikation und Validierung
Fachwissen: Erfahrung mit Stromversorgungen, Mikrocontroller-Sicherheitsmechanismen und weiteren Infrastrukturfunktionen von Hochvolt-Invertern
Problemlösung: Ausgeprägte Erfahrung in Trouble-Shooting, Root-Cause-Analyse und technischer Entscheidungsfindung
Sicherheit: Kenntnisse der funktionalen Sicherheit nach ISO 26262 sowie der Hochvoltsicherheit
Tools: Erfahrung mit Polarion, JIRA, Enterprise Architect und MATLAB/Simulink von Vorteil
Kommunikation: Sehr gute Englischkenntnisse, Deutschkenntnisse von Vorteil, sowie Reisebereitschaft nach Luxemburg von bis zu 25 %

Attraktive Konditionen: Unbefristete Vollzeitstelle mit einer Vergütung, die Ihrer Qualifikation und Erfahrung entspricht
Zukunftssichere Projekte: Übernehmen Sie technische Verantwortung für Hochvolt-Inverter und elektrische Antriebssysteme
Dynamisches Team: Kollegiales Umfeld mit kurzen Entscheidungswegen

Sr. IT Systems Engineer
Job Posted: June 19th, 2026
Location: EMEA
Hi there!
We're looking for a Sr. IT Systems Engineer to join our team. Zapier is on a mission to make everyone more productive at work. Zapier has helped millions of people build businesses through the power of automation.
This is an exciting role at Zapier in a growing team, and you will play a direct role in implementing and improving Zapier's IT infrastructure. Working closely with our Engineering, People Ops, and Security Teams, you will implement, manage, automate, and support the tools and services that power a globally distributed team.
We believe that a good IT experience is a perk -- it keeps people productive and engaged rather than getting in the way. You will help maintain a world-class Mac experience for our employees and streamline access management by implementing SSO applications and automating processes.

You will help scale our IT infrastructure and processes to the next level as a service owner, and you will be crucial to its success as Zapier grows. This isn't an IT Helpdesk job, but assisting and providing great customer service for Zapier's IT needs is part of the role.
If you're interested in launching your career at a fast-growing and profitable org, then read on...
Our Commitment to Applicants
Our Commitment to Applicants
Culture and Values at Zapier
Zapier Guide to Remote Work
Zapier Code of Conduct
Diversity and Inclusivity at Zapier
Zapier is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace dedicated to pursuing and hiring a diverse workforce.

Skilled IT Systems Engineer. We're looking for 3+ years of direct hands-on experience in the roll-out, maintenance, and support of an expanding IT infrastructure. Our fleet is all macOS.
Excellent communicator. We're a 100% remote team, and writing is our primary means of communication at Zapier.
Relationship-driven. You understand that building and maintaining trust across the organization is vital.
Creative and resourceful. You try as many angles as possible to implement simple and scalable IT solutions. You see the big picture but are pragmatic in implementing solutions that meet the needs of today.
Solid at time management. You'll balance a variety of fast-moving projects and pull the cord early when things go awry. As part of a distributed team, you are trusted to work with minimal supervision.
Growth-oriented. As part of a growing company, you have an opportunity to make an impact, and you're keen to build processes that'll make your job more efficient over time.
Things You'll Do
Zapier is a fast-growing and remote-first company, so you'll likely get experience on many different projects across the organization. That said, here are some things you'll probably do:
Implement SSO applications, manage onboarding/offboarding, and build automation workflows using Okta Workflows and Zapier.

Implement automated workflows to monitor and enforce license utilization across the SaaS portfolio.
Identify and act on rightsizing opportunities (unused seats, duplicate tools, tier mismatches).
Build and maintain reporting to surface spend trends, renewal risks, and optimization wins for leadership.
Partner with Finance and team owners to develop a strategy for maximizing value from SaaS investments.
Build tools and processes to eliminate manual work, automate user account creation, and integrate tools via API.
Resolve IT issues as they arise and build automations to eliminate recurring request patterns.
Perform provisioning and deprovisioning as part of onboarding/offboarding workflows.
Identify and implement enhancements to IT infrastructure and tooling.
Work across dozens of tools (Google Workspace, Jira, Slack, 1Password, Zoom, etc.).
Collaborate with the team to enhance and maintain the employee Mac experience.

At Zapier, we believe that diverse perspectives and experiences make us better, which is why we have a non-standard application process designed to promote inclusion and equity.

We're looking for the best fit for each of our roles, regardless of the type of education or companies in your background, so we encourage you to apply even if your skills and experiences don’t exactly match the job description.

All we ask is that you answer a few in-depth questions in our application that would typically be asked at the start of an interview process. This helps speed things up by letting us get to know you and your skillset a bit better right out of the gate. Please be sure to answer each question; the resume and CV fields are optional.

At IONOS, the leading European provider of cloud infrastructure, cloud services and hosting services, you will work together with a wide range of teams. We are characterized by open structures, a friendly working culture and flat hierarchies with a strong team spirit. We firmly believe that work and fun are compatible, and offer you the right environment for this. Our constant growth means that we are always looking for new colleagues. Become part of IONOS and grow with us.
Our DNS squad runs the naming, addressing and time services the rest of the internet quietly assumes will always be there: authoritative and recursive DNS, DHCP, forward proxy and NTP, together with the IP address management that ties them together. Our authoritative platform serves roughly 20 million zones from 12 anycast locations across two autonomous systems . Our DNS/DHCP/IPAM management system, DIM, is open source (github.com/ionos-core/dim) - what we build here, others run too.
Tasks

Operate, harden and evolve our authoritative and recursive DNS, DHCP, forward-proxy, DNS and IP Management (DIM) and NTP services so they stay boringly reliable at internet scale.
Automate everything that should be automated - infrastructure as code in Puppet, reviewed and version-controlled - and remove the toil that does not need a human.
Instrument and measure: build the metrics, dashboards and signals that tell us what our services are actually doing, because we cannot improve what we cannot see.
Drive root-cause analysis and lasting fixes through structured ITIL Incident, Problem, Risk and Change management - we make our work and our challenges transparent on purpose.
Take part in the team's on-call rotation for this KRITIS/NIS2 infrastructure (your turn comes up roughly once a month - mandatory and separately compensated) and use what you learn on-call to make the next on-call quieter.

Tools of the Trade
You will work with the protocol implementations and the tooling we use to deliver these services and keep them stable:
DNS / DHCP / proxy / time: PowerDNS (authoritative, recursor, dnsdist), ISC DHCP (experience with or appetite for Kea is welcome), Squid, chrony.
Platform & automation: Enterprise Linux 9, Puppet (GitOps), BIRD, rsyslog, collectd.
Languages: Python, Go, Java, Bash — plus the classic unix toolbelt (awk, sed, git) that still does more than people expect.
Data: ClickHouse, MariaDB, PostgreSQL.
You do not need to have mastered all of these on day one. You do need to be the kind of engineer who is comfortable reaching for the right one and going deep when it matters.

We care less about a perfect CV than about how you think. We work by a few principles, and we mean them:
"If you can't measure it, you can't improve it." We make data-driven decisions and monitor continuously.
"Do it once, do it right." Quality and attention to detail matter to us - shortcuts come back as incidents.
"Perfection is achieved not when there is nothing more to add, but when there is nothing left to take away." We strive for simplicity and efficiency in every solution; the best fix is often the one that deletes complexity.

Have operated DNS, DHCP or comparable network services in production, ideally at scale and under real reliability obligations.
Read RFCs for fun, debug with packet captures, and are not satisfied by "it works again" without knowing why it broke.
Automate by default and treat configuration as code.
Bring radical candor - say the uncomfortable thing early, in service of the work, not the ego.
Think in terms of blast radius. We use AI-assisted tooling in our development and test workflow, but production changes are always human-gated - risk awareness is a feature, not a brake.
If you have ever caused (or narrowly avoided) an interesting outage and learned something durable from it, tell us about it. That is operational experience, not a red flag.

Du arbeitest in einem vielseitigen Umfeld, in dem klassische IT-Infrastruktur, Cloud, Automatisierung und KI zunehmend zusammenwachsen.

We are Foundational
We're an early-stage, mission-driven startup tackling one of the hardest and most exciting engineering challenges in the space domain: building the most precise understanding of space and Earth using ground-based lasers.
Using satellite laser ranging (SLR) and space debris laser ranging (SDLR) data, we're giving the next generation of space companies exquisite orbital data - the foundation for resilient navigation, Earth observation, and precise space traffic control. This is essential infrastructure for the sustainability and resilience of the space domain, and we think it will be foundational to the future economy.
Our network doesn't stop at the ground. To close the loop on precision, we're building the small optical payloads that fly on-orbit and talk back to our stations, and the systems engineering that ties ground, space, and data platform into one coherent whole. That's where you come in.

This is a hands-on engineering role where the successful candidate will be as happy working in the lab as they are behind a computer. You'll work in our space team but may get involved in ground systems as well - helping to define what we build, model it, then get hands-on to build, test, and prove it.
You'll see the full lifecycle: early concept and trade studies, through modelling and design, into integration, environmental test, and validation against our ground network. It's physics-first, hands-on work with a quick path from your bench to orbit. You'll sit in a small team of software and hardware engineers who don't draw hard lines between disciplines, and you'll be expected to cross those lines too.

Systems engineering. Turning mission needs into requirements, interfaces, and budgets (mass, power, link, pointing, timing, error). Running trade studies and making the case for a design decision with numbers behind it.
Modelling & analysis. Building performance models - radiometry and link budgets, atmospheric transmission, pointing and attitude, detection probability - and using them to drive real design choices rather than to decorate them.
Design & build. Contributing to the design of small space-based payloads and ground subsystems: component selection, layout, tolerancing, and assembly of hardware and optical benches alongside our senior engineers.
Integration, test & verification. Assembling and aligning hardware, then putting it through environmental qualification (thermal, vibration, vacuum) and performance characterisation - and learning first-hand what survives launch.
Ground-to-space validation. Working with the ground systems team to validate ranging precision and pointing accuracy end-to-end, so the payload and the network behave as one system.
Owning your corner. Documenting designs, feeding lessons into the next iteration, and taking real responsibility for a slice of the system as we grow.

You don't need flight heritage or a decade of experience. We care far more about strong fundamentals, hunger, and the ability to learn fast in a hands-on environment.
Essential

Hands-on instincts. You like building, aligning, breaking, and fixing hardware, not only simulating it.
Scripting ability for analysis and modelling (Python preferred; MATLAB or similar is fine).
Comfort with ambiguity and ownership. You're energised by a startup where scope is broad, priorities shift, and nobody hands you a fully-specified task list.

Cutting-edge work. Meaningful, challenging, complex problems at the frontier of the space domain.

A team worth learning from. A dynamic, collaborative environment built on innovation, creativity, and teamwork - with room to grow fast.
A mission you can believe in. What we build underpins the future of Earth observation and space traffic control.

As a Business Systems Engineer on the GTM Engineering team, you will design, build, and operate the automation and AI systems that power ClickUp's Go-To-Market business — spanning core business products and the integration platforms that connect them.

You'll sit at the intersection of business systems architecture and applied AI — partnering with Sales, Finance, Revenue Operations, and fellow GTM Systems engineers to eliminate toil, accelerate revenue workflows, and build the automated, AI-augmented infrastructure the company runs on.

AI-Native Automation & Agent Development
Design and build AI-powered automations and agentic workflows across the GTM tech stack — including Salesforce, NetSuite, Workato, and MuleSoft — to eliminate manual effort and accelerate business operations.
Develop and deploy ClickUp Super Agents and LLM-based automations to automate tasks such as deal data enrichment, quote generation assistance, order validation, revenue recognition triggers, and exception handling in quote-to-cash workflows.
Architect and implement MCP (Model Context Protocol) integrations that allow AI agents to interact with business systems contextually and safely — enabling intelligent, event-driven actions across the GTM platform.
Explore and evaluate emerging AI capabilities (RAG, fine-tuning, multi-agent orchestration) and determine which are production-ready for GTM business systems use cases.
Build reusable AI templates, automation patterns, and agent blueprints that can be extended across the GTM Engineering team.
Business Systems Integration & Architecture
Build and maintain integrations across Salesforce, NetSuite, Workato, MuleSoft, DealHub (CPQ), and other GTM platforms — with a strong bias toward clean architecture, low technical debt, and supportable design.
Own end-to-end integration patterns for critical business flows such as lead-to-opportunity, quote-to-cash, order-to-fulfillment, and revenue reporting pipelines.
Design data flows and transformation logic that keep business data accurate, consistent, and accessible across systems without creating fragile point-to-point dependencies.
Apply a build-vs-buy mindset: evaluate whether a given automation need is best solved with native platform capabilities, iPaaS tooling, or custom code — and make the case clearly.
Platform Development & Tooling

Write automation scripts and data transformation logic in Python, JavaScript, or Apex as needed to bridge gaps that platform tooling cannot address natively.
Utilize Zapier, Workato, and similar iPaaS platforms to orchestrate cross-system workflows that are maintainable, observable, and well-documented.
Own the full lifecycle of what you build: discovery, design, development, testing, deployment, documentation, and ongoing optimization.
Reliability, Observability & Continuous Improvement
Monitor the health and performance of automations and integrations you own; proactively identify degradation, data inconsistencies, or failure patterns before they impact business operations.
Conduct root-cause analysis of integration failures or automation breakdowns and drive durable fixes — not just incident patches.

Gather feedback from business stakeholders and iterate on existing automations to improve accuracy, reduce edge cases, and adapt to evolving GTM processes.
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement
Partner with Sales, Revenue Operations, Finance, and Customer Success stakeholders to translate business requirements into well-scoped technical solutions.
Work closely with GTM Systems Engineering, DevOps, and BSA teammates on architecture decisions, intake prioritization, and delivery execution.
Contribute to the GTM Systems Engineering operating model: maintain task hygiene, communicate proactively on large initiatives, and log AI/automation work in the team's AI Excellence registry.

Experience deploying AI or LLM-powered automations in a production business systems context — or a clear, demonstrated trajectory toward it.

Ownership: You take full responsibility for the systems you build — from reliability and documentation to stakeholder trust and continuous improvement. You don't hand off and walk away.

At TACTILIA, we are building the industry-ready robotic hand that closes one of the biggest gaps in Physical AI.
